Hi Liam —

Thanks for the traffic sample — useful shape. High level answers up front, then a short commercial sketch below. Camila and Karthik are looped for the technical appendix.

1) Credits structure for a 3-month pilot: we recommend a "compressible credits" approach (see attached appendix) — commit to a pilot credit pool that is token-equivalent but tiered so unused committed tokens in month 1 can be converted into a smaller premium credit bank in month 2 (helps with bursty pilots). For your peaks (~6M tokens/day) a 90M-token month is a reasonable starting place for pilot scaling across regions.

2) Cache-first vs batch-first: given short queries with high repetition, choose cache-first. Prefix/KV caching gives the most unit-cost reduction for repeated prompts. We’ll enable continuous prefix caching + lightweight batching (2–8 requests) to preserve p95 latency.

3) Quantization recommendation: start with Q4_K (4-bit mixed scheme) for the initial pilot model family; that keeps p95 comfortably under 350ms on our N4i nodes for sequences in your sample. If you need more aggressive cost savings, we can move to a dynamic INT8 path for low-risk routes later in the pilot with a small quality regression budget.

Commercial sketch (pilot):
- 6-week pilot, 90M token-equivalent per month pool, convertibility rule between months.
- Pilot discount: 35% off list on standard token rates for the pilot consumption, plus a one-time operations credit to cover integration (~$6k).
- Post-pilot: option to convert commitments into a 12-month reserved band with staged discounts.

I'll attach a short appendix with the technical tradeoffs. Camila: can you add any tuning suggestions (latency vs recall) and a quick config we should pre-warm?

Ben
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference | Sales

Hi Liam —

Couple of practical config notes based on the CSV sample: short form bullets so your infra team can act quickly.

- Model variant: recommend "redwood-open-7b-q4k" as baseline. Empirically minimal generation divergence vs fp16 for short prompts.
- Cache policy: prefix caching enabled with a TTL of 24h for session prompts, and an LRU cap sized to ~1.5x your average unique prompt set (est. 50k keys). This keeps cold-starts rare.
- Batching: route latency-sensitive endpoints with max batch size 4 and prefer micro-batching (20–50ms accumulation window). Background batch jobs (analytics) can use larger batch sizes.
- Quantization fallback: serve primarily Q4_K; if a request hits a quality regression alarm (we’ll provide eval harness), route that request to an INT8_fallback pool for re-eval.
- Pre-warm: warm the KV cache by replaying your sample set at pilot start (Camila can provide a small harness). Expect prefix hit-rate to climb to 70–85% within 6 hours on steady load.

I'm attaching a two-page technical appendix describing kernel selection and expected p50/p95 numbers for your samples.

Cheers,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Compressible_Credits_Appendix.pdf (pdf, 210KB)

Nora — good constraints, thank you. Quick counter that preserves your $45k cap and gives predictable accounting:

Option A (capped, simple):
- Flat pilot cap: $45,000 for 6 weeks. We will translate the cap into a token-equivalent pool using a conservative token price for the selected Q4_K model. Any usage beyond the cap is paused unless approved.
- Discount: the cap reflects an implied ~42% discount vs list for expected consumption at the traffic you provided.
- Transition: if you convert to a 12-month commitment within 30 days post-pilot, we’ll credit 50% of unused committed tokens (if any) toward the first quarter of the new commitment.

Option B (compressible credits, more flexibility):
- Pilot commit: 90M tokens/month equivalent, compressible conversion rule between months. Pilot price with 35% discount; ops integration credit $6k applied upfront. If you prefer this but need the spend hard cap, we can add a monthly spend ceiling and provide weekly usage reports.

Security: we will share SOC2 Type II report and sign your security addendum. Link to security pack: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cRedwoodSecurityPack

If you prefer the procurement simplicity, Option A gives clear accounting and keeps your $45k requirement. If you're OK with a little more flexibility in operation and longer runway for burst management, Option B is slightly more cost efficient when the pilot is heavily cache-hit.

Happy to hop on a short call tomorrow to finalize.

Ben
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
